newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher on NCD issues.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher on NCD issues.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Monday as the central bank issued T$5 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess money and perhaps cool the sizzling stock market, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.417 percent against Saturday's 6.319 close, still well outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone, with commercial paper at 6.50 percent against 6.35-6.40.
Dealers said the central bank appeared to be taking steps to tighten liquidity with the aim of slightly cooling down the overheated stock market.
Dealers said they expected money rates to rise further as the delivery of T$30 billion in government bonds on Tuesday would tighten liquidity further.
The government bond market saw slow trade as bargain hunters hesitated to enter the market after the central bank continued to issue NCDs to absorb excess money.
The 10-year 86/4 bond yield closed at 6.1375 percent against 6.1375-6.1400 on Saturday.
Dealers said they expected the bond market to consolidate further if the central bank continues to issue NCDs to tighten liquidity. -- James Lin (2-5080815)
